Naive: cron on one server. A single point of failure that can't
Store executions in a DB partitioned by time bucket; a
poller fetches executions due in the next few minutes.
Two layers: the poller hands near-due jobs to a delay
queue that releases each one at its exact time, giving
second-level precision without hammering the DB.
Workers take jobs with a visibility timeout (lease). A
crash means the job reappears and is retried, so jobs
DB scan every few minutes → delay queue (SQS DelaySeconds ≤ 15 min, or a
Redis ZSET by timestamp) releases on time.
Lease expires and the job is retried. Heartbeats extend leases for long jobs;
Dedupe by execution_id at the queue or worker.
